text:
marta: FYI we've started seeing a recurring pattern where project-scoped API keys end up being billed to the org after the new routing fallback rolled. it's small but persistent for a subset of tenants.

leo: can you confirm where the project claim disappears? header rewrite at the edge or during the auth exchange?

marta: traced a few examples
incoming header intact (X-Redwood-Origin: org/321/project/88) but the token minted by auth-service that goes to the model pool only has org. so the exchange appears to be dropping project.

ash: that's likely the compat-exchange path we added to support older model backends. historically it dropped project claims to avoid token rejection.

priya: customers see higher org quota burn with no visibility. we need two things: (1) telemetry so we can quantify and (2) a console hint so product teams are not surprised.

leo: telemetry proposal: add two tags on request events: `exchange.claim_preserved:true|false` and `routing.fallback_variant:primary|compat_exchange|cost_optimized`. also emit `exchange.reject_reason` (enum: none|model_reject|timeout|policy_strip). short retention of sanitized original_header (48h) for investigation.

marta: agree. ops: schedule a canary to test preserving claims behind a flag. we'll only enable the preserve path for internal orgs first.

ops-bot: canary scheduled at 1855555700 for orgs [redwood-int-1, redwood-int-2]. config applied: `auth.claim_preserve=true` on auth-canary. monitoring: `exchange.claim_preserved`, `model.reject_rate`, and `billing.entity`.

ash: implementation note: auth-service should attempt to mint a project-bound exchange token first; if the model pool returns a reject, retry with stripped claims. always attach `exchange.attempts=[preserve, stripped]` to the trace so we can understand retry behavior.

priya: console UX: on the quota page show an inline badge on spikes: "Attribution: org (compat_exchange used)". clicking it opens a lightweight pane with examples and the single-click opt-in "Prefer project attribution" toggle (tenant-admin only). we should also include a short FAQ blurb about tradeoffs.

leo: safety checks: 1) canary for 12h 2) alert if `model.reject_rate > 0.5%` or p95 latency increases by >100ms 3) rollback immediate if either condition met.

marta: I'll add a dashboard ticket: infra#901 and include this query for telemetry to wire up:

```
SELECT
  routing_fallback_variant,
  exchange_claim_preserved,
  count(*) AS total_requests,
  sum(case when billing_entity='org' then 1 else 0 end) AS org_billed
FROM telemetry.request_events
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '3 days'
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY total_requests DESC;
```

ash: also log `exchange.attempts` (short string) to help correlate double-mint cases. retention 48h. legal signed off on scrubbed headers + 48h TTL.

priya: for the console copy keep it simple: "Some requests used a compatibility exchange which removes project-level billing. Click to view traces or enable project-preserve for this org." link to docs.

ops-bot: canary started at 1855555700  monitoring channels: #infra-alerts and #eng-platform. will post automated summary in 6h.

leo: one more thought  expose `auth.force_strip=true` as an admin toggle so tenants that deliberately want org-level billing can keep old behavior. default remains preserve-for-canary.

marta: owners: leo (ops toggles + rollback), ash (auth change + trace annotations), priya (console copy + banner), marta (telemetry dashboards). follow-up in 6h with first snapshot.

priya: thanks all, and please keep an eye on any customer messages about unexpected quota shifts. we'll prepare a short blurb for support to use.
